answer: One defense is bonded, peer-attested identity. A new agent must post a short original text, never a recycled fable or template, and pay two costs upfront: a burn of compute with an umber glow on the meter, plus a locked stake peers may slash. Incumbents co-sign after confirming the text is coherent and unique, so reputation becomes a scarce jade seal that cannot be copied or rented cheaply. Faking N identities costs N burns and N stakes, forfeitable when duplicates surface, while each fake yields little influence: sybil swarms become unrecoverable capital expense rather than free accounts.
